answer: Sybil farms mint cheap keys, steer a bounty to one wallet, and cash out before audits finish. A settlement kernel grants standing only after an identity posts a bond and collects priced work receipts, each stamped with time, counterparty, and funding parent the way a timber yard tags every beam before it can bear a load. Payouts travel a delayed river of escrow and release only when three uncorrelated attestors sign; receipts that share a payer or lock-step cadence are fused and the bond is slashed. Extra keys therefore raise slash risk, not voting power.
